public_rationale: The numerical component is supported: the reported SimpleQA hallucination rate was 37.1%, which rounds to 37%. The additional confidence claim is not established. SimpleQA counts even hedged contradictions as incorrect, so the aggregate rate does not show that more than one-third of responses were confidently false. Without the original responses or a confidence breakdown, the whole proposition remains unresolved rather than contradicted.
limitations: If 'confidently made up' is treated merely as informal shorthand for an incorrect answer, the numerical reading is supported.
The score concerns a particular benchmark run, not the frequency of errors in everyday ChatGPT use.
No conclusion is proposed for the separate parenthetical pricing comparison.

statement.excerpt: If you’re curious, OpenAI’s GPT 4.5 model — its most expensive general purpose LLM yet — flunked 37% of these questions. Which is, to say, that it confidently made up an answer more than one-third of the time.
statement.document_title: The Phony Comforts of AI Optimism

from_speaker: more than one-third of the time
our_interpretation: The questions are those in the original SimpleQA evaluation reported with GPT-4.5's launch.
Treat 37% as a percentage rounded to the nearest whole number.
The numerical claim concerns incorrect answers, not all answers that were not correct, which could also include abstentions.
'Confidently' ordinarily means presenting a false answer as reliable rather than expressly uncertain. It does not imply conscious deception.
The target is the February 2025 launch evaluation, not subsequent model versions or general ChatGPT usage.
The parenthetical pricing comparison is outside the supplied normalized proposition.
criteria.support_condition: The launch SimpleQA incorrect-answer rate rounds to 37%, and the evaluated responses establish that confidently incorrect answers occurred on more than one-third of all questions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The matched incorrect-answer rate does not round to 37%, or response-level evidence establishes that confidently incorrect answers occurred on no more than one-third of questions.

evidence.explanation: Incorrect answers can explicitly express uncertainty. This undermines the inference from an incorrect-answer rate to an equally large confident-error rate, but does not show what fraction of GPT-4.5's actual errors were hedged.
